chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them), that they said:

The capital of the orphan's wealth has no zakat due upon it in the principal (al-'ayn) and the silent/accumulated portion (al-samit); as for the profits/gains (al-ghallat), then upon them is obligatory charity (zakat).

key_terms.الصَّامِتِ: The silent/accumulated portion (wealth that has not yet generated profit)
key_terms.الْغَلَّاتُ: Profits or gains derived from the capital

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying zakat on an orphan's wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the Ahl al-Bayt clarifies the juristic distinction between the principal capital (al-'ayn) and its silent accumulation (al-samit), which are exempt from zakat, while profits (al-ghallat) are subject to it. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh as it protects the wealth of minors and the mentally incapacitated from immediate taxation, ensuring their capital remains intact for their future benefit. It reflects the practical application of zakat principles to dependent classes, emphasizing growth over static possession.
